Commentary.Commentary: We are back for South Africa Under-19's reply. Zimbabwe U-19 players can be seen in a huddle before they make their way out on the field. Followed by the opening pair of South Africa Under-19 in Lhuan-dre Pretorius and Steve Stolk. It is going to be Anesu Kamuriwo to start with the first new ball.
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, South Africa Under-19 would feel they have an easy task on their hands, but they need to apply themselves really well here. If Zimbabwe Under-19 are able to start well with the new ball, then even 102 could seem to be a huge score. You never know, it is cricket after all. Do join us shortly for the second essay.

Kwena Maphaka, the man of the moment is in for a chat. He says that he is very happy with his performance and is glad he could pick those wickets for his team. He further more says that it has been a good journey so far and will look to finish on the high. He ends by saying that the wicket is still good for batting and they will chase it down easily as they have been batting really well throughout the tournament so far.

Although, post the first drinks break, the change of bowlers inspired the comeback for South Africa Under-19. Tristan Luus and Riley Norton applied the squeeze really well. They kept piling up the pressure with the dot balls, which eventually resulted in wickets for them. Once the 53-run stand for the fifth wicket was broken, there was no real fight shown apart from the final 20-wicket stand. The tail-enders chipped in with some to take the score above 100. Tristan Luus chipped in with three wickets for South Africa Under-19, while Riley Norton ended up with a wicket to his name.

Zimbabwe Under-19 just did not turn up with the bat in hand. They were put under pressure inside the first 5 overs itself, as they ended up losing 4 wickets in no time. It was looking grim for them, but then came a stand between Ronak Patel and Ryan Kamwemba, which did some repair work for them, and despite losing 4 wickets, they made sure that they set the tone of this innings, and kept scoring boundaries at will. They took the score to 60/4 at the end of Powerplay 1. One would've though this is a good platform for the batters to work on, although it was not the case here. The first five overs were dominated mostly by Kwena Maphaka, with the new ball, who eventually ended the day with a five-wicket haul to his name. The second time in this tournament.

Well, utter dominance by the South Africans with the ball in hand. They were outstanding from the start. Never allowed the Zimbabwe batters to catch their breath. Although, they were frustrated for the final wicket which almost took 9 overs for the final partnership to break. In the end, Zimbabwe Under-19 could only get 102 on the scoreboard. This is also the highest score by Zimbabwe Under-19 while batting first in this tournament, will it provide them with the needed edge over their opponents? I doubt so.

OUT! CAUGHT! That is the end of the Zimbabwe Under-19 innings! Tristan Luus finishes things off and gets rid of Mashford Shungu. Pitches the ball up on the stumps and Mashford Shungu looks to go over the top but mistimes the ball straight up in the air. Raeeq Daniels gets under the ball and completes the catch running to his left from mid off. Zimbabwe Under-19 are all out for 102 runs in 29.2 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: Right then! The Players and the Umpires are on the field to start the game. Zimbabwe Under-19 has been asked to bat first by South Africa Under-19 and its Panashe Taruvinga and Nathaniel Hlabangana to open the batting for them. Kwena Maphaka has the new ball in hand and will start the attack for South Africa Under-19. Let's Play!
The players and the Umpires are lined up on the field for the National Anthems. Its Zimbabwe's National Anthem followed by South Africa's National Anthem.

PITCH REPORT - The dimension are 68m and 65m on either squares. Tino Mawoyo informs that the breeze is coming through nicely and should help the players a lot. States that the surface is dry, probably could get some turn as the game progresses. He feels that 220-230 should be a good score on this wicket.

The captain of Zimbabwe Under-19, Matthew Schonken joins in now. Starts by saying he feels they are positive, and would've batted first anyways. Mentions that they are looking forward to this game. States that the batters need to bat deep, because South Africa have a very good bowling attack. In the end, informs that they have a couple of changes to the team.

Juan James, the captain of South Africa Under-19 is in for a chat. Says that he is looking to bowl first as the conditions get better as the game progresses and they would want to use their bowlers  first up. In contrast, Zimbabwe Under-19 has endured a mixed tournament, clinching victory in only one of their encounters thus far. Despite a convincing eight-wicket win over Namibia, they faltered against formidable opponents, suffering defeats at the hands of Australia by a staggering 225 runs and Sri Lanka by 35 runs. Eager to redeem themselves, Zimbabwe enters the Super Six stage with a hunger for success, eyeing a turnaround in fortunes as they prepare to challenge South Africa in what promises to be a riveting clash of cricketing prowess. Having commenced their campaign on a high note with a commanding 31-run triumph over the West Indies, South Africa Under-19 suffered a setback, succumbing to a 36-run defeat against England. However, they swiftly bounced back in their previous encounter, overpowering Scotland by seven wickets to secure a berth in the Super Six stage. Notably, Steve Stolk's blistering knock of 86 runs off 37 balls, adorned with seven boundaries and eight sixes, propelled South Africa to victory, instilling confidence in the team as they gear up to face Zimbabwe Under-19.

A warm welcome and greetings to all the cricket enthusiasts worldwide, joining us today! The stage is set for an exhilarating encounter as South Africa Under-19 prepares to face off against Zimbabwe Under-19 in their inaugural Super Six match of the ICC U-19 World Cup 2024. This match will be played at Senwes Park in Potchefstroom. With the group stage done, 12 teams remain in contention for the ICC U19 Men's World Cup 2024 as the tournament enters the Super Six phase. Senwes Park, renowned for its neutral pitch conditions, promises an equitable platform for both bat and ball. While the surface offers consistent bounce, ideal for aggressive stroke-making, it tends to curtail seam movement, making it less favorable for swing bowlers. As the match progresses, the pitch can evolve into a batting paradise, particularly advantageous for teams chasing targets.
... MATCH DAY ...

It's time for the Super Six stage of the 2024 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup and we have breezed along to game no.6 as Zimbabwe Under-19 takes on the hosts South Africa Under-19 at the JB Marks Oval, Potchefstroom. The hosts South Africa Under-19 courtesy of topping their group have walked into this game high on confidence. The side won a couple while losing 1 to England Under-19 in the group stage. If the last game they played is a sign of things to come then fasten your seatbelts as these young Proteas can blow away any opponent on their day. The side chased down a mammoth total of 269 without even breaking a sweat in just 27 overs against Scotland Under-19 in their last group-stage game. The dynamic duo of Steve Stolk and Lhuan-dre Pretorius at the top is working wonders for them while the middle order is well equipped with quality batters in Tristan Luus, Dewan Marais and David Teeger. The side does possess some destructive finishers and all-rounders in Richard Seletswane and skipper Juan James. Young Protea bowlers have been doing their bit as well as the side has carried a couple of points to the Super Six stage thanks to their victory against the Windies in the group stage. Zimbabwe Under-19 on the other hand sits at rock bottom with zero points to to their name as they were defeated by both Australia Under-19 and Sri Lanka Under-19 in the group stages. The side advanced to the Super Six courtesy of their victory against Namibia Under-19 in their last game. Their batting unit has struggled against the opponents but Panashe Taruvinga came as a ray of hope for them in their last game and the side would be counting on him to lead the batting attack in the Super Six stage against some of the heavyweights in their group. The bowling unit though has been decent enough with Ryan Simbi and Newman Nyamhuri picking up 6 each in the group stage games and skipper Matthew Schonken would be counting on them again. Can South Africa Under-19 continue to impose themselves on their opponents or will we see the first major upset of the tournament? We shall find out when these sides collide.
